ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (revised on November 8, 2024, effective January 1, 2025); Administrative Measures for the Filing of Beneficial Owner Information by Legal Persons, Unincorporated Legal Persons and Individual Industrial and Commercial Households (People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation Order No. 3, effective November 1, 2024); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision); Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Tax Collection; Measures for the Registration Administration of Foreign-Invested Enterprises; and the Cross-Strait Agreement on Investment Protection and Promotion applicable to the Taiwanese investor.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the parent non-resident investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the parent investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Single-path authentication: if the issuing registry is in a Hague Apostille Convention state, notarize the document and obtain only a Hague Apostille from that state's competent authority; if the issuing registry is in a non-member state, notarize the document and obtain consular legalization from the PRC embassy or consulate in the issuing jurisdiction. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Existence) of the parent investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or designated government authority in the parent investor's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille-only for documents issued by an Apostille Convention member state; consular-legalization-only for documents issued by a non-member state. No sequence combining both shall be used.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney appointing the WFOE legal representative and local manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the parent investor, attested by the company secretary and notarized locally
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the resolution in the parent jurisdiction; if that jurisdiction is an Apostille member, annex a single Hague Apostille; if it is a non-member, complete consular legalization at the PRC consulate. Parallel paths and no chaining.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (constitutional documents) of the parent investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent investor certified by its registered company secretary or notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy must be notarized and then receive either a Hague Apostille (member state) or PRC consular legalization (non-member state); never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming account relationship, signatory authority and good banking history
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank maintaining the parent investor's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer signature must be notarized; the notarized letter then receives either a Hague Apostille if the bank is in an Apostille state, or PRC consular legalization if the bank is in a non-member state. The two authentication routes are alternatives and never cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial ownership declaration and certified identity documents of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent investor and relevant government identity registry or notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The declaration is signed by each UBO, identity documents are notarized, and the package is legalized through the single applicable path: Hague Apostille or PRC consular legalization, depending on the issuer's location; do not layer both.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Conduct mandatory screening of each UBO, director, shareholder, senior manager, and authorized signatory against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, PRC List of Terrorists and Extremists (Ministry of Public Security Announcement No. 15 of 2015), PBOC beneficial-owner information repository, and Cross-Strait restricted/ineligible investor lists. The compliance officer must identify PEPs, immediate family members, and close associates of domestic and foreign PEPs, apply enhanced due diligence, verify source of funds, and document any negative news. Screening must be refreshed at incorporation and prior to bank account opening, with audit trail retained for no less than five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Online Declaration and Registration System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Chinese names must be registered in simplified Chinese characters; traditional characters, English letters, Arabic numerals, and Pinyin are accepted only as auxiliary or transliterative elements, not as a substitute for the Chinese statutory name. The doctrine requires a four-tier corporate name: administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry or business objective + legal form. The foreign investor's company name must be transliterated into a standard Pinyin form unless a recognized Chinese translation already exists in the SAMR database. The trade name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any prior name in the same industry within the same administrative district, and the English auxiliary name must be declared.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must obtain the SAMR written rejection notice with legal basis. The applicant may first correct the proposed name and file a new online declaration immediately, without fee. If the rejection is legally disputed, the applicant may file a written Administrative Reconsideration Application with the superior SAMR within 60 days from receipt of rejection, stating name structure, evidence of non-confusing similarity, industry code, and compliance with the Company Name Registration Administration Provisions. If reconsideration fails, the applicant may initiate an administrative lawsuit in the competent People's Court within six months. Extensions are generally not available beyond the 30-day name reservation window, but a new reservation may be filed for the same corrected name after the prior reservation expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox as the sole registered office is highly likely to be rejected by SAMR, municipal tax authorities, and corporate bank account officers. For a WFOE engaged in direct online retail of portable battery generators and solar panels, the company must maintain a physical leased or owned premises in the registered administrative district where core records, management personnel, and operational equipment exist. A virtual mailbox may be accepted only as a supplementary notification address where the WFOE also holds a physical office; pure virtual addresses are not accepted for tax registration or bank account opening because the tax authority requires an on-site inspection and the bank requires a physical due-diligence visit. Customs and battery storage requirements also favor a warehouse or serviced office with storage capacity. Recommendation: lease a serviced office or small warehouse/showroom that can host inspections and inventory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: front-door signage matching the WFOE Chinese name; lease agreement under company name; current utility invoices at the registered address; presence of office equipment, inventory records, e-commerce back-office server or logins; labor contract and employee records; tax registration certificate; business scope and e-commerce website; board resolution for address use; customs or dangerous goods storage permits for solar batteries. Quantified risk: moderate-to-high, approximately 40% annual probability of at least one unannounced on-site inspection by municipal SAMR, tax, or market regulation authority for a WFOE in online retail of power storage products; likelihood rises to 65% if an anomaly appears in VAT declarations, export refunds, or name and address inconsistency reports.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAMR enterprise name reservation and WFOE incorporation registration government fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and local municipal market supervision bureaus
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official national fee for ordinary limited liability company registration; only de minimis local printing or card fees may apply.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the parent investor's corporate documents (certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, board resolution or power of attorney, articles of association, bank reference letter)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed notary public in the parent investor's home jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial tariff for a multi-instrument corporate package; USD 450-1,200 depending on document volume and translation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille certification for each document issued by an Apostille Convention member state
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent Authority designated by the issuing Apostille state
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: State-fixed apostille fee per document plus agency convenience fee; approximate USD 10-60 per apostille and USD 150-300 package agency fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization of documents from a non-Apostille state (parallel alternative to Apostille; never chained)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Embassy or Consulate General of the People's Republic of China in the parent jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Chinese consular legalization fee schedule per document; approximately USD 80-200 per document plus translation and courier services.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PRC counsel pre-incorporation due diligence, UBO piercing report, name clearance filing, and apostille or consular authentication review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Engaged PRC law firm or licensed corporate secretarial service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a WFOE Stage 1 package ranges from USD 2,800-5,500 fixed fee, excluding disbursements.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Twelve-month registered physical office lease (serviced office or warehouse/showroom acceptable for e-commerce plus battery storage)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial landlord or property company under a lease executed in the registered administrative district
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rental benchmark for a 30-60 square meter serviced office and approved storage area; approximately USD 800-1,300 per month plus property management fees.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Reserve for translation, courier, document retrieval, and bank account opening due diligence support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translation agency, international courier, and support service providers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Disbursements-only benchmark under PRC market rates; USD 300-800 depending on document volume and jurisdiction.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act of Taiwan (consolidated version), Chapter II, Articles 1-23; Article 128 (company limited by shares); Article 154 (single-member limited liability); Article 156 (share issuance and paid-in capital); Article 192 (election and powers of directors); Article 216 (supervisor); Article 387 (registration). Also applicable: Business Registration Act, Articles 4-7; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 4, 8 and 12; Enforcement Rules of the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Article 3.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), acting through the MOEA One-Stop Company and Commercial Registration System; foreign investment approval and screening is performed by the Investment Commission, MOEA under the same one-stop portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application Form for a company limited by shares, accompanied by the notarized or certified Articles of Incorporation, CPA capital verification report, incorporation meeting minutes or sole-shareholder written resolution, Foreign Investment Approval Letter, registered office address proof, and director/supervisor consent forms.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Taiwan Companies Act does not impose a minimum paid-up capital on an ordinary company limited by shares. For CN_WFOE_LTD, the sole shareholder will subscribe 1,000,000 ordinary shares at NT$10 per share, for an aggregate initial paid-in capital of NT$10,000,000. No blocked escrow account is required; however, the subscribed capital must be remitted from overseas through an authorized foreign-exchange bank into a temporary Taiwan investment account, remain intact until the CPA issue of the capital verification report, and not be withdrawn before company registration. Withdrawal, asset misappraisal, or false payment before registration triggers criminal liability and personal liability of directors under Articles 9 and 11 of the Companies Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF CN_WFOE_LTD, a company limited by shares incorporated under the laws of Taiwan, R.O.C.

WHEREAS the sole shareholder has subscribed for 1,000,000 ordinary shares at a par value of NT$10 per share, for aggregate paid-in capital of NT$10,000,000, and the said capital has been remitted and verified in accordance with the Companies Act and the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals; and

WHEREAS the Foreign Investment Approval Letter was duly issued by the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, approving 100% foreign ownership of the Company;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by unanimous consent of the duly elected board of directors, that the incorporation acts and preparatory transactions of the subscriber, incorporating attorneys, and certified public accountants, including the adoption of the Articles of Incorporation, the reservation of the Company name, the approval of the business scope of direct online retail of portable battery generators, solar panels and related accessories under ISIC 4791, and all related expenditures, are hereby ratified, approved, and confirmed in all respects.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be and hereby is fixed and adopted at [Insert Full Physical Address, Taipei City, Taiwan], and that the board instructs counsel to prepare and file all documents necessary with the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs to register such office as the statutory domicile of the Company, and to use same for tax, labor insurance, civil process, and government correspondence purposes.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the following persons are hereby appointed as the first statutory officers of the Company: [Director/Chairman Name] as Director and Chairman; [Director/General Manager Name] as Director and General Manager; [Supervisor Name] as Supervisor; and [Chief Financial Officer Name] as Chief Financial Officer, each to serve for a term of three years and thereafter until successors are duly elected and qualified. The Chairman and General Manager, or either of them acting jointly with the Supervisor, are hereby authorized as statutory representatives to execute and deliver contracts, leases, permits, applications, and other instruments on behalf of the Company.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Company open and maintain its principal operating and revenue accounts at CTBC Bank Co., Ltd. and Taiwan Business Bank Co., Ltd., and that any two of the Chairman, General Manager, and Chief Financial Officer be and hereby are designated as authorized signatories, with authority to sign account opening forms, specimen signature cards, checks, wire transfer instructions, foreign exchange settlement documents, electronic payment mandates, and all bank security instruments; the Board further ratifies the corporate cards and online banking signatory matrix to be filed with each bank.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Board directs management to apply for all operational and industry licenses, including business registration, Uniform Invoice / VAT registration, customs import-export registration, fire-safety and civil-defense approvals, environmental registration or exemption, and any warehouse occupation permits necessary for the e-commerce fulfillment and product storage operations, and to retain Taiwan counsel for this purpose.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that this resolution shall take effect immediately, and that the corporate secretary is instructed to retain a true copy in the corporate minute book and to file a certified copy with the Company Registration Application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Foreign Investment Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA One-Stop Company and Commercial Registration System (https://gcis.nat.gov.tw) for name reservation; Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (https://investtaiwan.tw) for foreign investment approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name and business-scope search on the MOEA commercial registration information platform and reserve the exact legal name, including an English version, for the company. Concurrently prepare and submit Form A foreign investment application through the Investment Commission's one-stop portal, stating that the Taiwan entity will be 100% foreign-held and will engage in ISIC 4791 direct online retail of portable solar power equipment and battery generators. The application must include the corporate shareholder's certificate of incorporation, board resolution, audited financial statement or bank reference, business plan, and negative-list declaration. The Investment Commission will issue a Foreign Investment Approval Letter after completing beneficial-owner screening. The letter must be obtained before any company registration filing and before the central foreign-exchange remittance.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application through MOEA portal
Form A foreign investment application
Certificate of incorporation and apostille/certification of the foreign corporate shareholder
Board resolution of the foreign shareholder authorizing investment
Audited financial statements or bank reference letter of the investing shareholder
Business plan for e-commerce retail of solar panels and portable battery generators
Declaration that no Taiwan negative-list industry is involved
Power of attorney in favor of Taiwan counsel
Beneficial ownership and politically exposed person identification forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed company name is rejected due to similarity, the applicant must file an administrative name amendment through the same MOEA portal and reserve an alternative name; if the Investment Commission issues a query, a supplementary response must be filed within 14 days with corrected or additional evidence, legal opinion, or a revised Form A. Failure to respond will result in withdrawal, but a new application may be refiled after cure without loss of priority if submitted within 30 days of the suspension notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting Articles and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Taiwan-licensed certified public accountant registered with the Financial Supervisory Commission; final validation through the Commercial Registration Division, Department of Commerce, MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage Taiwan corporate counsel to draft the Articles of Incorporation in compliance with the Companies Act, including company name, registered office location, ISIC 4791 business scope, share classes, authorized capital, issued capital, board size, supervisor appointment, meeting quorum, and accounting year. Have the sole shareholder execute a written resolution approving the Articles and the proposed statutory officers. Open a temporary Taiwan investment account at an authorized foreign-exchange bank, remit NT$10,000,000 or an equivalent foreign currency amount from overseas, and secure the bank's foreign-exchange settlement record. A Taiwanese CPA then performs capital verification and issues a statutory report certifying that the full share consideration has been received, is unencumbered, and is held in the company's bank account. Execute and notarize the incorporation meeting minutes or sole-shareholder written consent, and prepare the registered office lease or ownership evidence.
required_dossiers: Approved Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Final draft of the Articles of Incorporation
Sole shareholder written resolution approving the Articles
CPA capital verification report
Bank remittance and foreign-exchange settlement certificate
Registered office lease agreement or ownership certificate with landlord consent
Incorporation meeting minutes or shareholder written consent appointing directors and supervisor
Consent to act forms executed by each director, supervisor, and general manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CPA declines to verify capital due to foreign-exchange or anti-money-laundering concerns, the remittance must be returned and re-remitted through an authorized foreign-exchange bank with a corrected purpose code; if MOEA queries the capital adequacy, the board may adopt an amended resolution to reduce paid-in capital and file an amended Articles of Incorporation, recalculating the CPA verification and registration fee before formal filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Company Registration and Business/Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs; after issuance, local National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance for business registration and Uniform Invoice / VAT obtaining
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete company registration file to MOEA using the Company Registration System under the company-limited-by-shares module, with all electronic documents signed by the applicant or Taiwan counsel. MOEA will cross-check the name reservation, business scope, foreign investment approval, capital verification report, and director/supervisor qualifications. After registration fee payment and successful review, MOEA issues the electronic Company Registration Certificate. Within 15 days of the certificate date, apply at the local National Taxation Bureau for business registration, tax identification number, Uniform Invoice registration, seal registration, and employer withholding file. All online retail sales, including cross-border e-commerce transactions, must be recorded under this tax registration.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Application Form
Articles of Incorporation as approved and verified
CPA capital verification report
Incorporation meeting minutes or shareholder written resolution
Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Registered office address proof
Consent to act forms and identification documents of directors and supervisor
Power of attorney for Taiwan counsel
Business registration and Uniform Invoice application forms
Company seal and Uniform Invoice seal registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues a suspension for missing documents, the applicant has 14 days to cure through the electronic portal. If the tax bureau queries the registered office or lease, the company must submit a landlord use-consent letter, building usage license, or an amended lease. Failure to obtain business registration within the statutory window is cured by late filing with penalties, but if the company registration is voided, the entire incorporation package must be resubmitted after correcting the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation and Labor/Tax Registration Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Selected Taiwan banks (CTBC Bank and Taiwan Business Bank); National Health Insurance Administration; Bureau of Labor Insurance, Ministry of Labor; local National Taxation Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the corporate operating account by presenting the Company Registration Certificate, Board Resolution, specimen signature cards, and identification of the authorized signatories. The bank will finalize the digital banking mandate, payment gateway onboarding, and anti-money-laundering due diligence. Register the company with the Bureau of Labor Insurance for labor insurance, employment insurance, and labor pension, and with the National Health Insurance Administration for the first employees. The company must register its employer tax withholding file with the tax bureau before issuing the first payroll. If e-commerce payment rails Stripe and Affirm BNPL are to be used, the bank must confirm that the company's settlement account accepts card-present and card-not-present payments and recurring billing receipts.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Board Resolution authorizing bank account opening and signatories
Specimen signature cards of Chairman, General Manager, and CFO
Tax Identification Number registration certificate
Business Registration and Uniform Invoice certificate
National Identification or passport copies of authorized signatories
Labor insurance and health insurance employer registration forms
Employment contract and payroll system documentation
Payment gateway onboarding forms for Stripe and Affirm BNPL
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank declines the mandate due to incomplete beneficial-ownership information, the board must issue an amended resolution and submit updated passport and source-of-funds declarations. If the labor insurance authority imposes late registration penalties, the company may appeal within 30 days by proving the actual date of first employment with payroll records and employment contracts. If Stripe or Affirm BNPL account onboarding is delayed, provide the ratified signatory matrix and final bank confirmation letter to the payment processors for manual review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Fire-Safety, Environmental, Customs and Warehouse Operational Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Economic Development Bureau or Department of Economic Development of the local special municipality/county government; local Fire Department; Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan; Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance; and the Occupational Safety Research and Health Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the e-commerce fulfillment warehouse and temporary storage of portable lithium-ion battery generators and solar panels, obtain the warehouse operating permit or commercial facility registration from the local municipality or county government. Submit a fire prevention plan, fire-safety equipment layout, and emergency response protocol to the local Fire Department, and obtain a Fire Safety Facility Approval for the storage area. File an environmental self-certification or exemption letter with the Environmental Protection Administration or local environmental protection bureau as appropriate. If the company later holds goods in a customs-bonded warehouse, register with the Customs Administration under the Bonded Warehouse measures. All battery storage areas must satisfy occupational safety requirements, including ventilation, thermal-runaway containment, electrical inspection, racking structural certification, and staff training records.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Business Registration and tax identification number
Warehouse lease with legal use certificate
Warehouse floor plan and structural load/stamping certification
Fire safety equipment installation and maintenance certificate
Fire prevention and emergency response plan
Environmental registration, exemption, or self-certificate filing letter
Waste disposal contract with a licensed industrial waste treatment operator
Customs import/export registration certificate (where applicable)
Occupational safety and health hazard assessment report
Material safety data sheets for lithium-ion battery products
Civil-defense or civil protection plan if required by the local Fire Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the local fire department or environmental agency issues a deficiency letter, hire a licensed fire-safety technician and an environmental engineering consultant to submit a corrective action plan within the stated cure period. If the warehouse use does not conform to the building-use permit, apply for a building-use change or a temporary use certificate before re-filing. If any license is denied due to missing information, refile with additional landlord consent, updated floor plans, and professional certifications; appeals to the ministerial administrative review committee are available within 30 days of an adverse decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs for industrial policy and special permits; local special municipality/county/city Economic Development Bureau for warehouse and commercial operation licensing; local Fire Department for civil-defense and fire-safety approval; Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan for environmental review and waste regulation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Registration License and Uniform Invoice/VAT registration; Warehouse/Logistics Facility Operation Permit (or commercial facility registration) issued by the local Economic Development Bureau; Import/Export Customs Registration; Fire Safety Facility Approval Certificate; Occupational Safety and Health Facility Management Certificate; and, if applicable, Bonded Warehouse Registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan (EPA Taiwan) with local environmental protection bureaus acting as review agencies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full Environmental Impact Assessment for a low-impact e-commerce retail warehouse and distribution center with gross floor area below 5,000 m², no manufacturing, no solvent degreasing, no significant wastewater discharge, and no operation in an environmentally sensitive area. If gross floor area equals or exceeds 5,000 m², or the facility performs lithium-battery recharging/training, repair, or bulk repacking, a Category C Preliminary EIA / Environmental Registration is required; a full Category A or B EIA Report is triggered only for large logistics complexes or hazardous waste treatment operations not contemplated by this ISIC 4791 retail scope.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: domestic sanitary discharge below 100 m³/day requires no separate water pollution discharge permit, but must comply with public sewer discharge standards (pH 6-9, COD ≤ 200 mg/L, SS ≤ 100 mg/L). If daily design wastewater flow reaches 100 m³ or more, a Water Pollution Control Permit is required with effluent limits of pH 6-9, COD ≤ 100 mg/L, and SS ≤ 30 mg/L. VOCs: the intended retail-warehouse activity involves negligible volatile organic compound emissions; if solar-panel adhesive application, battery electrolyte exposure, or solvent cleaning is ever introduced, annual VOC emissions above 600 kg require an Air Pollution Control Permit and must meet Taiwan's stationary-source emission standards, including general BACT and HAP compliance, using low-VOC materials and capture devices. Hazardous waste: spent lithium-ion batteries and damaged solar panels must be classified under the Waste Disposal Act as general industrial wastes or regulated electrical and electronic waste; the facility must store such waste in fire-rated containers, mark and segregate it, contract with a licensed waste processor, retain disposal manifests for at least three years, and file an annual waste clearance plan with the local environmental protection bureau.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety: the warehouse must obtain a Fire Safety Facility Approval Certificate from the local Fire Department covering fire alarm systems, smoke detectors, fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, exit signage, and fire-resistant storage; the company must file a fire prevention plan and an emergency evacuation plan as part of the Civil Defense program. Occupational Safety: the company must perform a baseline occupational hazard assessment under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, provide electrical safety inspection for battery charging areas, maintain ventilation and thermal-runaway control, obtain structural certification for storage racks, and conduct employee emergency-response training. The Civil Defense clearance includes registration of hazardous chemical storage locations with the local fire department if lithium-battery stock exceeds the threshold requiring emergency response planning, and the company must maintain first-aid supplies and an accident-spill response kit.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Taxation Bureau of Taiwan (Ministry of Finance) - Electronic Tax Filing Portal: https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity (e.g., a Chinese WFOE) establishing a taxable presence in Taiwan, the entity must apply for a Business Registration (營業登記) with the local National Taxation Bureau. The procedure includes: (1) submitting a completed Business Registration Application Form (營業登記申請書) to the competent tax authority in the jurisdiction of the business premises; (2) providing the original and copies of the company's incorporation certificate, articles of incorporation, and proof of foreign registration; (3) submitting a power of attorney (授權書) authorizing a local representative or tax agent; (4) providing the lease agreement or proof of ownership of the business premises; (5) obtaining a Uniform Invoice Number (統一編號) which serves as the Tax Identification Number (TIN) for VAT and income tax purposes. The application can be filed online via the Ministry of Finance's e-tax portal or in person. Approval typically takes 5-10 business days. The entity must also register for the electronic invoice system if it engages in B2C retail sales.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (Taiwan does not offer check-the-box elections; foreign entities are taxed on a territorial basis for income tax, but for indirect tax purposes, the entity is treated as a taxable business. No hybrid mismatch elections are available under Taiwan's tax law.)

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Monthly sales exceeding NT$80,000 (or annual sales exceeding NT$960,000) triggers mandatory registration for Business Tax purposes. However, for foreign e-commerce sellers, registration is required regardless of threshold if they have a fixed place of business or a dependent agent in Taiwan.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates the use of Electronic Uniform Invoices (電子發票) for all B2C retail transactions. Sellers must integrate with the Ministry of Finance's Electronic Invoice Integration Platform (財政部電子發票整合服務平台) to transmit invoice data in real-time or within 48 hours. For certain high-risk industries, real-time clearance via API is required. Anti-fraud digital stamping (QR code and random number) is mandatory on all electronic invoices. Failure to comply may result in penalties and suspension of business.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the export of goods from Taiwan to foreign countries (including mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau) and to services provided to foreign enterprises or individuals that are used outside Taiwan. For goods, the seller must provide proof of export, such as a customs export declaration (出口報單) and a bill of lading. For services, the seller must provide a contract and evidence of foreign currency receipt. The zero-rating is claimed on the Business Tax return, and input VAT on related purchases can be refunded.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading (提單) or Airway Bill
Inward Remittance Certificate (外匯收入證明) or Foreign Exchange Receipt (結匯證明)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau conducts rigorous audits on zero-rated transactions. If the required documentation is incomplete or fraudulent, the zero-rating is disallowed, and the tax authority will assess the 5% Business Tax retroactively, plus a penalty of up to 5 times the underpaid tax. Additionally, interest is charged from the original due date. In cases of deliberate fraud, criminal liability may be pursued under the Tax Collection Act, leading to imprisonment or fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), exercising delegated foreign-exchange administration under the People's Bank of China
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: RMB is freely convertible on the current account once the supporting trade or service documentation is verified by the domestic bank, while capital-account transactions are strictly controlled. For a CN_WFOE_LTD receiving equity subscription proceeds from a Taiwan shareholder, the funds must be wired into a foreign exchange capital account opened after the FDI foreign exchange registration with SAFE. The bank monitors the use of every capital injection and permits conversion into RMB only for genuine business expenditures under the payment-use mechanism after contracts and invoices are reviewed. Dividend remittance to the Taiwan parent is treated as a current-account outflow, but the bank will require an audited annual financial statement proving that the profit is distributable, a board resolution declaring the dividend, enterprise income tax clearance of the dividend withholding obligation, and documentary evidence that prior audited losses have been fully recovered. There is no legal prohibition on remitting the entire after-tax profit to Taiwan, but without the required audit and bank-level economic substance review, the remittance will be held. The WFOE should not attempt to convert capital-account receipts into RMB and later remit them as dividends before the scheduled operational usage; that would be deemed a disguised capital outflow and trigger penalties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: In accordance with SAFE current-account regulations, export proceeds from the sale of solar portable power products must be repatriated to the domestic collecting bank within 180 days after export declaration, unless an extension is approved by SAFE for certified receivables. There is no mandatory conversion percentage; the WFOE may keep the full amount in foreign currency in a current-account foreign exchange settlement account or convert 100% to RMB at the daily price. The bank must cross-match each MT103/CIPS credit to the customs declaration and the e-commerce transaction background in the cross-border payment database before settlement. Failure to meet the 180-day receipt requirement subjects the entity to a lower trade facilitation category and blocks export tax rebate claims.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Escrow Account and RMB Basic Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Basic Operational Account and Export Settlement Account
FDI Capital Escrow Account and Trade Settlement Account
Cross-Border E-Commerce Settlement Account and RMB Basic Deposit Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable as a primary banking channel. PRC law requires the WFOE to hold its operating RMB account and SAFE-registered foreign exchange capital account at a licensed domestic commercial bank. Offshore digital EMIs are legally barred from opening domestic Chinese bank accounts or settling SAFE-controlled transactions. Stripe and Affirm are merchant checkout rails only; their settlement funds must be transferred into a licensed third-party payment institution and then swept into the WFOE tier-1 bank account. The EMI cannot be used as the corporate treasury account, FX conversion point, or payment clearing backbone.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch presence is mandatory for the mainland finance director and the account signatories when opening the RMB basic account and activating the SAFE capital account. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted. If the Taiwan statutory director cannot travel, the WFOE must appoint a mainland-based responsible person holding a notarized and apostilled power of attorney; the branch compliance team will also arrange a video-call identity and interview verification with the statutory director at the Taiwan parent bank office or a designated Taiwan law firm before the account can be used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border ownership chain ending in Taiwan with intermediate offshore holding companies, creating ambiguity over the true beneficial owner and the economic origin of the equity funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled certificates of incorporation and register of members or certificate of incumbency for each intermediate entity; an ownership diagram signed by the ultimate shareholder; biographical, passport and tax residence records of the ultimate beneficial owner; audited group financial statements for the last three years; bank reference letters from the Taiwan parent clearing bank; and a sworn declaration confirming no adverse PEP, sanction or litigation positions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FDI capital injection funded by intra-group borrowing, warehouse finance or third-party lending rather than demonstrable accumulated profit, suggesting round-tripping or disguised capital flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution for the capital contribution approved by the Taiwan parent; the approved WFOE business plan and expenditure projection; remitting bank statements showing the lawful accumulation of funds; the underlying loan or warehouse facility agreement and lender regulatory license; a repayment-capacity balance sheet and bank confirmation letter; the SAFE foreign direct investment registration certificate; and a notarized undertaking that the capital is being injected as equity and not as undisclosed debt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags inherent in cross-border e-commerce of portable solar generators, where declared retail value, settlement amounts, shipping routes and customs declarations may mismatch.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original commercial platform settlement reports and merchant IDs from Stripe and Affirm, including order IDs, refunds and fee deductions; logistics waybills and customs declaration records reconciled to each settlement batch; supplier invoices from the Taiwan party; VAT and corporate income tax filings; product documentation and independent price benchmarking reports supporting the invoice value of the respective solar panel and battery generator models.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, restricted-party, geographical and adverse-media screening flags from operating across a Taiwan/China corridor with cross-border payment flows to banking hubs used by the parent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: World-Check or Dow Jones Factiva screening results for every director, senior manager, beneficial owner and material counterparty; a compliance counsel memo explaining false-positive matches; transactional country-coding evidence showing no nexus with sanctioned jurisdictions; customer and supplier restricted-party lists; and a board-approved sanctions, geoblocking and transaction-monitoring policy implemented inside the payment stack.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan parent must execute a SWIFT MT103 using the beneficiary bank details of the CN_WFOE foreign exchange capital account, with the remittance purpose code stated as Foreign Direct Investment Equity Subscription and the SAFE FDI registration reference quoted in the payment instructions. The receiving tier-1 bank validates the incoming credit against the SAFE filing before booking it, and then a Chinese registered CPA performs capital verification and issues a legal capital verification report confirming paid-in capital. After verification, the foreign currency can be converted into RMB and transferred to the RMB basic operational account only as the WFOE presents underlying invoices, contracts, payroll schedules and tax filings supporting the approved purpose. Remittances must not be split to circumvent SAFE threshold filings, and any excess contribution over the registered foreign-invested amount requires an amended FDI registration before funding.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operating and trade payments, the WFOE issues a SWIFT MT103 payment instruction through its tier-1 bank, quoting the correct SAFE current-account payment purpose code and attaching the commercial invoice, purchase order, bill of lading or air waybill and customs declaration. The bank debits the RMB account, performs spot FX conversion, and sends the wire through the correspondent clearing network. For major import shipments of solar panels and portable power systems from Taiwan, the preferable rail is an irrevocable commercial letter of credit opened under UCP600 with a clean bill of lading, packing list, certificate of origin, quality inspection certificate and commercial invoice as required documents. Documentary collections on D/P or D/A terms can be used for recurring low-value deliveries once a clean settlement history exists. For RMB-denominated trade, CIPS may be used instead of SWIFT MT103 if the Taiwan counterpart bank participates in CIPS, reducing correspondent bank costs and keeping clearing within the PBC system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forwards with a licensed domestic commercial bank, limited to the amount and tenor of underlying USD/RMB current-account exposure from export sales or import purchases.
Onshore FX swaps between RMB and foreign currency to manage short-term trade-liquidity timing, supported by the real trade documents and board-approved treasury policy.
Currency options and zero-premium collar structures for the WFOE actual settlement flows, restricted to genuine exposure and approved by the bank compliance desk.
Cross-currency swaps are permissible only when the underlying is a SAFE-registered loan or long-term trade payable; speculative or leveraged swap structures are prohibited.

Offshore RMB non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted for the onshore WFOE; an NDF hedge, if needed, must be executed by the Taiwan parent outside the China entity and cannot be booked, paid or reimbursed by the WFOE.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Bureau (jurisdiction of the Taiwan headquarters registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: From 1 May to 31 May immediately after the close of the calendar year under assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an ad valorem additional tax of 3% of the assessed unpaid tax for each two-month period of delay, capped at 10%, plus post-due interest at the statutory Ministry of Finance annual rate (currently applied on a daily basis); prolonged non-filing permits the tax authority to make an estimated assessment, refer the debt to the Administrative Enforcement Agency for compulsory execution, and, where the company becomes inactive or fails to cure after notice, the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) may order dissolution and strike-off under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business (Value-Added) Tax Periodic Return - six bimonthly returns forming the Taiwan VAT annual filing cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The 15th day after the end of each two-month VAT period: Jan-Feb due 15 Mar; Mar-Apr due 15 May; May-Jun due 15 Jul; Jul-Aug due 15 Sep; Sep-Oct due 15 Nov; Nov-Dec due 15 Jan of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file on time allows the National Taxation Bureau to compute the tax on an assessment basis and impose a late penalty of up to 15% of the tax determined, together with daily interest on overdue payment; habitual non-filing and non-payment will be escalated to administrative enforcement, asset freeze, and may be treated by MOEA as cessation of business, leading to a dissolution order and eventual deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Withholding and Non-Taxable Income Statements (Salary and remuneration payee listings)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Bureau (via electronic filing gateway)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January of the year following the withholding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file withholding statements subjects the company to a penalty of NT$150 per statement, not exceeding NT$60,000 per taxable incident, plus recovery of unpreserved withholding tax and interest; disregard of enforcement notices is referred to the Administrative Enforcement Agency and the non-compliant company is exposed to MOEA dissolution action for failure to maintain lawful corporate operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and filing of annual financial statements with the corporate registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce (or regional central corporation administration office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be approved by the shareholders within six months after fiscal year end (by 30 June); the approved copies, including CPA-audited statements where compulsory audit thresholds are met, must be filed with MOEA within 15 days after approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve and file statutory accounts after administrative notice gives MOEA the power to impose fines on responsible directors and, if the default continues, to order dissolution of the company; the WFOE may also be disqualified from foreign-investor profit remittance until the filing is made.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign investment operation report (investor's annual report on the invested Taiwan entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Investment Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year end (by 31 March for a calendar-year company), unless extended in writing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or late filing may brand the foreign investor as non-compliant with the Foreign Investment Act, causing rejection of subsequent share transfer or capital remittance applications, suspension of foreign investment approval, and, after repeated notice, cancellation of the foreign-invested status; this can in turn lead MOEA to deem the underlying corporate registration defective and to commence administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporation amendments and registered-office/register updates (annual maintenance to reflect continuing changes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days of each occurrence for director, shareholder-contribution, manager, registered address, or constitutional instrument changes; no separate Taiwan annual return is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late amendment registration is punishable by fines under Company Act Article 387-2; more importantly, third-party protections and foreign-investor approvals may be lost, and MOEA may issue a dissolution order when the company is notified repeatedly for registry non-compliance and remains unresponsive, triggering deregistration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Company Act Article 20(2) and the MOEA/FSC implementing rules, a non-public Taiwan WFOE limited company must have its annual financial statements audited and certified by an independent Taiwan CPA if at fiscal year-end any one of the following quantitative thresholds is met: (a) paid-in capital is NT$30 million or more; (b) outstanding borrowings and credit facilities from financial institutions amount to NT$30 million or more; (c) annual operating revenue for the reporting period reaches NT$50 million or more; or (d) the competent authority specifically requires an audit. The thresholds are applied to the company's consolidated amounts and are reviewed annually by MOEA in consultation with the Financial Supervisory Commission.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Applicable accounting standards for financial statements are the Financial Supervisory Commission-endorsed IFRS for companies required to follow FSC rules; non-public companies are permitted to prepare their statutory accounts under Taiwan Business Enterprises Accounting Standards (Taiwan EAS/local GAAP) or IFRS as endorsed by the FSC, and tax-basis reconciliations must be provided in the Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not operate a stand-alone annual UBO filing portal for ordinary WFOEs; instead, the company must continuously keep its shareholder register and ultimate beneficial ownership information current at the registered office, and each shareholding transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members immediately and, where the foreign-investor status is affected, reported to the Investment Commission within 30 days of completion. Any change triggering a company registration amendment must also be submitted to MOEA within 15 days. The information is confirmed annually when the shareholders approve the financial statements and, in practice, when the foreign investor files its annual foreign investment operation report.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 9,000 per annum only if the statutory compulsory audit threshold is exceeded; below threshold, no CPA audit is required, but preparation compliance may incur USD 1,000 - USD 2,500 from an outsourced accounting service

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: China standard CIT rate is 25%. Small Low-Profit Enterprises (SLPEs) with annual taxable income up to RMB 3 million enjoy an effective 5% rate (25% reduction of taxable income and 20% tax). High and New Technology Enterprises (HNTE) pay 15%. R&D expenses are eligible for a 100% super-deduction. No patent box regime currently exists; certain free-zone income may benefit from preferential rates (e.g., Hainan FTP 15%).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return, Type A) filed via the State Taxation Administration’s electronic tax bureau portal (e-tax), typically the 'Electronic Settlement and Payment System'.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly interim prepayments using Form A200000 paid within 15 days after the quarter-end)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed and finally settled within five months after the fiscal year-end (May 31 for calendar-year enterprises). Quarterly prepayment returns are due within 15 days after each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales revenue from online retailing of portable solar power stations, generators, batteries, and solar panels.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all gross receipts from B2C and B2B online sales, including those to overseas customers. For cross-border e-commerce, export sales that satisfy customs supervision are still taxable for CIT at the WFOE level. Disclose any related-party sales to the Taiwan marketing entity and ensure the profit allocation is at arm's length. Retain customer records, payment gateway settlement reports (Stripe, Affirm), and logistics contracts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales, including procurements of solar modules, portable generators, packaging and freight.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When purchasing from a Taiwan-affiliated supplier, adopt the CUP or cost-plus method to determine the transfer price. Include customs duties and non-deductible VAT. The cost base must be verified by bills of lading, customs declarations, and intercompany purchase orders. Do not overstate purchases to shift profits to a tax haven or a low-tax jurisdiction.

Management fees, intra-group service fees, or royalties paid to the Taiwan parent are deductible only if such services are actually rendered and are beneficial to the WFOE. Provide a service agreement, evidence of cost allocation, and a report on the economic substance of services. Otherwise, the expense will be added back to taxable income and may bear late-payment interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total profit for the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the accounting profit determined under the PRC Accounting Standards. Before arriving here, any dividend, interest, or royalty payments made to non-residents during the year should have been properly recorded with withholding tax deducted. If a permanent establishment exists in Taiwan, allocate income to it and compute the Chinese foreign tax credit, but only if treaty benefits are properly documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after legal adjustments, including non-deductible expenses and tax-exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back intercompany service fees lacking substance, excessive entertainment expenses, interest on thin-capitalized loans, and any portion of expenses paid to non-residents that was not subject to withholding. Subtract eligible tax credits. The resulting amount is the base for at 25% (or preferential) rate. Maintain full documentation for all adjustments affecting cross-border payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final income tax payable after credits, prepayments, and incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% headline rate, or the reduced 15% HNTE / 5% SLPE effective rate. Any withholding tax on non-resident distributions is not shown here; it must be remitted via a separate withholding tax declaration (Form F002) at the time of payment. Non-resident shareholders’ dividends are not reduced by any DTA as the Cross-Strait Agreement has not entered into force.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7: Related-Party Transaction Schedule (Part G of Form A100000 supplementary filing)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed disclosure of all related-party transactions, including equipment purchases, advances, royalties, and service fees with the Taiwan parent and other affiliates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory if any related-party cross-border transaction exists. Report the amount and pricing policy for each category. This schedule is a focus of tax audit and transfer pricing investigations. Failing to disclose accurately triggers a deemed assessment and penalties under Special Tax Adjustment rules (Circular 42 of 2016).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: base penalty of CNY 2,000; severe cases CNY 2,000 - 10,000. Late payment: daily interest surcharge of 0.05% on the unpaid tax. Fraudulent underreporting: penalty of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax, plus criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 203 if the tax evaded exceeds RMB 50,000 and is more than 10% of the tax due, or RMB 100,000 and more than 30%; imprisonment up to 7 years. Failure to withhold non-resident tax triggers a fine of 50% to 300% of the un-withheld amount (Law on Taxation Administration, Article 69).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax on dividends remitted to non-resident shareholders (including Taiwanese shareholders). No reduced treaty rate is available because the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (signed in 2015) has not yet been ratified and entered into force.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Under the (currently ineffective) Cross-Strait Tax Agreement, a resident of Taiwan would need to obtain a Taiwan Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Ministry of Finance, complete a Beneficial Ownership Self-Declaration, provide evidence of substantive business activities (employees, offices, bank accounts) in Taiwan, and file an advance application with the PRC tax authority in charge of the WFOE before the dividend distribution. Without an effective agreement, no treaty reduction can be applied at the time of dividend payment. If the agreement is ratified domestically, the standard protocol for treaty relief will apply, and the claimant must submit the TRC and a letter of residence to the state tax bureau along with the withholding return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory and treaty rates: 10% on cross-border interest and royalties paid to Taiwanese residents (no treaty relief available). Royalties for the use of IP owned by the Taiwan parent are taxable at 10%, and the payer must withhold before remittance. Interest on intercompany loans that exceed the thin capitalization limit (2:1 debt-to-equity for non-financial enterprises) will be disallowed as a deduction and may be recharacterized as a dividend, triggering 10% WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File (同期资料本地文档) preparation is required if any of the following annual related-party transactions are exceeded: (i) tangible asset transfers > RMB 200 million; (ii) intangible asset transfers > RMB 100 million; (iii) financial asset transfers > RMB 100 million; (iv) other related-party transactions > RMB 40 million. The Master File (主体文档) must be prepared when cross-border related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion. Annual related-party transaction report (Form A100000 schedules) is mandatory regardless of amount for any related-party structure.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China applies substance-over-form principles under General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR, Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law) and the Special Tax Adjustment Measures (Notice
